Method of Attack: Injecting custom malicious emails inside Email Encryption Appliances (EEAs) by discovering the EEA's IP address and injecting malicious payloads that bypass email security gateways (ESGs).
Bypassing ESGs by exploiting network topology and email flow between ESG, EEA, and email servers.
Using MIME-encoded payloads including ransomware, macro-malware, phishing links, and password-protected archives.
Masking attacker origin by spoofing EEA IP address in emails to ESG.
Impacted Systems: Email servers running Email Encryption Appliances (EEAs)
Attack Vector: Inbound SMTP connections to Email Encryption Appliances (EEAs)
Direct injection of malicious emails into EEAs after discovering their IP addresses
